x: A is correct: devaluation, import tariffs and export incentives all switch demand from foreign to domestic goods, so they are expenditure-switching measures. B is a mix (reduced government spending and higher interest rates are expenditure-reducing, though import quotas are switching), while C and D contain only expenditure-reducing fiscal and monetary measures.

The Economic Survey 2025-26 traced the stagnation in merchandise exports to petroleum and gems-and-jewellery exports; non-petroleum, non-gems-and-jewellery goods, which make up 78.7% of merchandise exports, were not the source of the stagnation.
Since independence India has run a trade surplus in only two years, 1972-73 and 1976-77; in every other year imports exceeded exports.

Pairs 2, 3 and 4 are correct, so C. Pair 1 is wrong: devaluation is the official lowering (not raising) of a currency's value under a fixed regime; official raising is revaluation. Depreciation and appreciation are market-driven rises and falls in the rupee price of foreign currency under a floating regime.

B is correct: EHTP units deal in electronics hardware and get duty-free inputs. EOUs cover goods generally (not only software), STPs cover software (not agricultural machinery), and an SEZ is itself a designated duty-free enclave, whereas it is EOU/EHTP/STP units that can be located anywhere.
